analysis: Of 256 rules with parameters <= 4, 220 are certified terminating (218 by matrix interpretations, 2 by the conservation theorem), 28 carry verified loops, 8 remain unknown. H-C03-2 is contradicted by 12 loops; H-C03-1 and H-C03-3 are not contradicted by any certified status.
assumptions: loop search = forward closures with right and left extensions, words <= 40 letters, <= 40000 closure pairs
matrix interpretations over N: d = 2 (entries 0..4) and upper-triangular d = 3 (0..3), d = 4 (0..1)
falsification: A loop certificate for a rule predicted terminating, or a termination certificate for a rule predicted non-terminating.

history.new: Of 256 rules with parameters <= 4, 220 are certified terminating (218 by matrix interpretations, 2 by the conservation theorem), 28 carry verified loops, 8 remain unknown. H-C03-2 is contradicted by 12 loops; H-C03-1 and H-C03-3 are not contradicted by any certified status.

hypothesis: Three competing hypotheses are tested. H-C03-1 (naive): terminates iff s <= p or r <= q (some letter count never grows). H-C03-2 (director's first guess): terminates iff r < 2q or s < 2p. H-C03-3 (after the first loops): non-terminating iff s > p, r > q and (r >= 2q or s >= 2p).
methodology: For each rule: (1) proven regions by counting (s < p or r < q) or conservation (s = p or r = q); (2) forward-closure loop search, every certificate re-checked step by step; (3) if no loop, exhaustive matrix-interpretation search, certificate re-checked in exact arithmetic; (4) otherwise bounded evidence: reachable sets from all words of length <= 12 containing the left-hand side.
question: Which rules 0^p 1^q -> 1^r 0^s terminate, and what separates terminating from looping rules?
title: Termination survey of the 256 rules 0^p 1^q -> 1^r 0^s (p, q, r, s <= 4)
